description: Reader-side test that turns a voxel's votes into blocked or not: at least min_hits hits and a hit share of at least min_hit_share. BlockedRule::any_hit() is the safest mode. The writer never applies it.

Bounded record of coalesced chunk keys per publication generation. Each reader keeps its own cursor. A cursor older than the retained window returns ChangeHistoryLost and the reader resyncs from a snapshot.

Proposed published form (plan D5 option d, D12 option c): 2 bits per voxel for unknown, free or blocked, derived in the writer from the votes by a configured rule. Only chunks where a class flipped are copied at publish.
Finite sensor-to-hit grid traversal. Positive-length interior cells emit Free. The endpoint voxel emits exactly one Hit. Tied plane crossings step together, so edge and corner touches are omitted.
A chunk whose working contents have changed since its last successful publication. Publish snapshots these keys and then clears the set.

Snap each source and hit to its voxel and trace one ray per unique voxel pair. The centre-to-centre form was dropped (2026-10-21) because it erodes surfaces near voxel boundaries; the surviving form is Pair-hint.
Optional ray lever (plan D11). The hit is applied at the true endpoint, but free votes go only to voxels within R metres of the source, so space beyond R stays unknown until the vehicle comes closer.
Hits divided by all votes (hits + misses) in a voxel, between 0 and 1; read as the voxel's probability of being blocked. Votes::hit_share in src/live/votes.rs.

Replaceable RayUpdateModel that adds a hit or free delta and clamps. Unknown cells start at zero and are still marked observed. Probability conversion stays outside ingestion. It is a reference formula, not the project's sensor model.
One point in point mode, or one source/hit pair in ray mode. A ray can update many voxels; the observation count stays one.

Vote decay configured with VoteDecay on VoteModel (plan D7, src/live/votes.rs). At each publish, every voxel updated since the previous publish has its counts scaled by keep (Exponential) or halved once past the cap (CapHalving). The result is order-independent between publishes, and unobserved voxels are never decayed.

Optional ray lever (plan D3). Within a scan, each unique source-voxel to hit-voxel pair is traced once along its first ray's exact path, and that path receives the pair's ray count as votes. Every ray still counts; only the path is shared. Requires vote counts.

The writer copies only dirty chunks into immutable Arc snapshots and installs them in the reader index under one write lock. Readers see this generation, which can lag the working map. An empty publish leaves the generation unchanged.
Immutable chunk snapshots available to any number of SceneReader handles. A cell is visible here only after a successful publish.

Optional inclusive Euclidean distance test from a ray or point-batch sensor origin to the hit, implemented with precomputed squared bounds and no square root. Rejecting the hit rejects the whole observation and writes no voxels.

How the planner learns the map changed under its path (plan D6). On each new published generation it rechecks the voxels in its path's clearance corridor against its own blocked rule, instead of tracking changed chunks.
Proposed dense voxel array of fixed extent centred on the vehicle and scrolled as it moves (plan D13, D10). It gives GPU kernels flat storage and bounds memory.

expansion: Per-scan cell deduplication with hit precedence
description: OctoMap-style rule: within one scan each cell gets at most one Free or one Hit, with the Hit taking precedence. Withdrawn as plan D2 (2026-10-21) because it drops votes and every ray must count.

One complete sweep of the sensor's scan pattern, for example one revolution or one hemisphere coverage, every 100 ms for the user's sensor. The application publishes once per completed pass (plan D6).

Proposed design: several writers, each the sole owner of a disjoint set of chunks. Every shard applies rays in input order, so per-cell order holds without locks. A coordinator publishes all shards under one generation.

Surface voxels turned free by rays that pass through them at grazing angles toward other hits. It comes from the update rule rather than from DDA precision, and it creates false free space for a path planner.
A voxel the active update model has never written. Readers return None. In ray mode a stored numeric zero remains observed and is distinct from unknown.

Decided ray model (plan D1), implemented as VoteModel and Votes in src/live/votes.rs. Each voxel stores u32 misses (rays crossing it) and hits (rays ending in it). Addition commutes, so the map is identical in any ray order. Readers apply a Blocked rule.
The mutable chunk map owned by the single PointSceneWriter or RaySceneWriter. Insert paths take &mut self and do not lock this map.
